latest_nl_proof:
Let I_{n,j} denote the half-open interval [j/n,(j+1)/n). Define J_{n,j}:[0,1/n)→I_{n,j} by J_{n,j}(d)=j/n+d.

First, J_{n,j} is well-defined into I_{n,j}: if d∈[0,1/n), then 0≤d<1/n, so
j/n ≤ j/n+d < j/n+1/n = (j+1)/n.
Hence J_{n,j}(d)∈[j/n,(j+1)/n)=I_{n,j}.

Second, J_{n,j} is injective: if J_{n,j}(d_1)=J_{n,j}(d_2), then
j/n+d_1 = j/n+d_2,
so d_1=d_2.

Third, J_{n,j} is surjective onto I_{n,j}: given any x∈I_{n,j}, set d=x-j/n. Since x∈[j/n,(j+1)/n), we have 0≤x-j/n<1/n, so d∈[0,1/n). Then
J_{n,j}(d)=j/n+(x-j/n)=x.
Thus every x in I_{n,j} has a preimage.

Therefore J_{n,j} is a bijection from [0,1/n) onto I_{n,j}. Moreover, the inverse map is exactly x↦x-j/n, because for d∈[0,1/n),
(J_{n,j})^{-1}(J_{n,j}(d))=d,
and for x∈I_{n,j},
J_{n,j}((J_{n,j})^{-1}(x))=x.
So the inverse function is x↦x-j/n.
role_in_parent: Packages the left-endpoint normalization as an explicit affine correspondence.
statement_nl: Let n be a positive integer and j an integer with 0 <= j <= n - 1. The affine map J_{n,j}(d) = j/n + d is a bijection from [0, 1/n) onto I_{n,j}; its inverse is x -> x - j/n.

domain_restrictions: n is a positive integer, so 1/n is well-defined and positive
j is an integer constrained by 0 <= j <= n minus 1
the affine map is defined on the half-open interval [0, 1/n)
the codomain/target is the interval I_{n,j}
the inverse formula x maps from I_{n,j} back to [0, 1/n)
statement_semantic_sketch.normalized_claim: For every positive integer n and every integer j with 0 <= j <= n minus 1, define J_{n,j} from [0, 1/n) to I_{n,j} by J_{n,j}(d) equals j/n plus d. Then J_{n,j} is a bijection onto I_{n,j}, and the inverse function is: given x in I_{n,j}, the corresponding preimage is d equals x minus j/n.
quantifier_order: for a fixed positive integer n
for a fixed integer j satisfying 0 <= j <= n minus 1
